newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - July 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - July 29.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Australian Football League club Richmond Tigers has sacked its coach Robert Wallis following the team's 137-point loss to Adelaide at Football Park which prompted club president Leon Daphne to withdraw his public support for Wallis. Page 20.

Australian Rugby Union Wallaby coach Greg Smith reversed an earlier decision and included fly-half David Knox in his starting line-up for Saturday's Tri-nations Test against South Africa in Brisbane. Page 20.

According to Australian Rugby Union Wallaby veteran Simon Poidevin, the Australian team is playing outdated rugby and will not compete successfully with the dynamic New Zealand All Blacks until they change their style. Page 20.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Australian soccer team Sydney United chairman John Hewson has accused Soccer Australia of having a secret agenda with its threat to expel the Pumas for bringing the game into disrepute. The board of Soccer Australia is expected to announce its decision ater it meets on Saturday. Page 46.

Australian rugby club Penrith Panthers beat the Euro League leaders Bradford Bulls 54-14 in a World Club Challenge match at the Penrith Stadium last night to move into quarter-final contention. Page 45
The Australian Rugby Union will have to tolerate having at least one Australian Football League match played in direct competition with the Bledisloe Cup schedule in Melbourne in 1998. Page 44.
THE AGE

The Australian Football League Tribunal has found Port Adelaide captain Gavin Wanganeen guilty of a charging violation against Ben Doolan by field umpires Andrew Coates and Gavin Deller. Wanganeen will sit out Saturday's scheduled game with league leader Geelong. Page B8.

Australian Football League team Brisbane Lions is expected to lose player Michael Voss for the rest of the season due to a serious knee injury following X-rays confirming he had torn the posterior cruciate ligament in his right knee. Page B8.

Australian basketball player Luc Longley has established a foundation for disadvantaged children. Longley, who currently plays with the Chicago Bulls, will contribute all A$200,000 of his off-court earnings into the Luc Longley Foundation. Page B8.
THE HERALD SUN

According to Australian basketball coach Ian Stacker, his team has the ability to win the gold medal at this week's under-23 championships despite losing to the United States and Lithuania last week. The team is expected to be strengthened by the inclusin of National basketball draftee Chris Anstey. Page 92.

According to Essex secretary-general Peter Edwards, Australian cricket player Stuart Law is likely to retain his overseas import spot ahead of Australian Test star Mark Waugh who is currently playing in the Ashes against England. Page 93.

Australia is one wicket away from winning the fourth Ashes Test to take a 2-1 series lead. This has increased the pressure on England's captain Mark Atherton, with several London newspapers suggesting his imminent replacement in the top position. Page 9
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Canberra Raiders' coach Mal Meninga was less than impressed with the performance of referee Robert Connoly accusing him of trying to be the focal point of the game despite his team winning 42-12 against Halifax. Page 60.

New South Wales will field a strong team at the Australian Women's Interstate Teams Series at Melbourne's Commonwealth Golf Club in August to be led by state champion Adele Bannerman, the No1-ranked player in Australia. Page 59.

Australian Rugby League's Manly coach Bob Fulton has stepped up calls for the introduction of video replay referees following confirmation that a legitimate try by the Sea Eagles was disallowed during a game against Parramatta last week. Page 61.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
